newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES OUTFIELDER ERIC DAVIS HAS COLON CANCER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES OUTFIELDER ERIC DAVIS HAS COLON CANCER.

text.p: Baltimore Orioles outfielder Eric Davis, who had surgery Friday to remove part of his colon, has learned that the extracted mass was cancerous, the team announced on Tuesday.

At this time, it appears the cancerous tumour was confined to the colon and apparently was removed with the extracted part of the intestine, the team said. Davis, 35, continues to recuperate at Johns Hopkins.
"I am feeling well and looking forward to making a full recovery," Davis said through the team, which held a news conference before Tuesday night's home game against Montreal.
"I would like to thank my family, all of the fans, my teammates, my friends, the Orioles' organisation and the staff at Johns Hopkins for all of the support they have given me.
"I have been following the team very closely and I am very excited to see that we are doing so well. I hope to be back on the playing field as soon as I possibly can."
Davis has resumed eating solid food and should be ready for discharge from the hospital in the next few days. He is being evaluated for possible chemotherapy.
Davis, who hasn't played since May 25, originally was expected to be sidelined for eight weeks, but the team did not give a new timetable, if any, for his return.

The talented outfielder, known for his explosive offensive combination of speed and power, was hitting .302 with seven homers and 21 RBI in 34 games for the first-place Orioles, who are a major league-best 45-20.

Davis, who retired after the 1994 season with a herniated disk in his neck, enjoyed a stellar season with Cincinnati last year after a one-year absence, batting .287 with 26 homers and 83 RBI. Davis has also excelled on defence, having won three Gold Glove awards.
